narrative.overview:
Price Radar is a light operate dashboard. The own shop price is the bench on every product card: a violet wash holds that price beside a small sparkline, marketplace rows sit under it as gaps, and a tinted sentence names the undercut. The ground is a cool grey, cards are white with a hairline and one soft shadow, and the loud color is the gap itself. Red means a marketplace is cheaper. Green means the shop is. Marketplace hues stay on the series dot and the chart stroke.

The page is a scan, dense and quiet. One sans, Inter, with the system stack behind it when Inter is not installed. Figures are tabular, in German formats. `color-scheme` is light. There is no dark theme.

The card does the job without a chart. The history chart opens in a side panel. The product photo sits in a rounded frame with the name beside it, and it carries no caption.
keyCharacteristics: Cool grey ground, white cards, one shared soft shadow
Violet marks the shop; red and green mark the gap
Marketplace hues stay on the series, each with its own dash
Inter at 14px, tabular prices and percents, German formats
Shop block, marketplace rows, and the undercut sentence are the card

rules.name: The Shop Bench Rule
rules.body: Violet is the own shop: the block, the chart series, the reference cell, and text links. Marketplace hues never color it, and violet never means "cheaper" or "failed."

rules.name: The Gap Rule
rules.body: A gap under −0.05% is Undercut Red. A gap over +0.05% is Shop Green. Inside that band the pill is Mute Slate on Soft Fill. A missing or failed price is a dash, never a guessed number. The sentence uses Undercut Ink or Green Ink, not the pill color.

rules.name: The Series Rule
rules.body: A marketplace keeps one hue and one dash on every card and on the chart. Amazon Amber and Fetch Amber stay different colors.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Inter is the face. The system stack is only the fallback. Monospace is for the shop URL, because it is an identifier, and for nothing else.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Prices, percents, SKUs, and dates set tabular numerals. Money uses a German format with two fraction digits and a trailing €. Percents use one fraction digit, a leading + when the marketplace is dearer, a true minus (−) when it is cheaper, and ± inside the flat band.

rules.name: The Scan Grid Rule
rules.body: Product cards flow at a 300px minimum, 14px apart, inside the 1360px column. Below 600px they stack, and the filter bar scrolls sideways instead of wrapping.

rules.name: The Resting Shadow Rule
rules.body: Cards, KPIs, and panel boxes share the resting shadow. Menus, tooltips, and the panel use their own deeper shadow. Do not invent a second resting shadow.

rules.name: The Bar Blur Rule
rules.body: The only backdrop blur is the sticky filter bar: the ground at 88% over transparent, blurred 10px. Cards stay opaque.

rules.name: The Soft Corner Rule
rules.body: 16px for the card, 12px for an inset block, 9px for a control, full round for a gap pill. Do not square the cards, and do not round the page itself.

rules.name: The Sparkline Rule
rules.body: On the card, the sparkline is the cheapest marketplace, colored by the gap, and the dashed mute line is the shop price. On the panel chart, the shop series is the violet stroke and each marketplace keeps its own hue and dash.

dos: Do keep the ground cool grey and the cards white, with the shared resting shadow.
Do measure every marketplace price against the shop price, and show the gap as red, green, or mute.
Do keep each marketplace on its fixed hue and dash, on the row dot and on the chart.
Do show a missing or failed price as missing: a dash in the pill, and a mute or amber note. Never a filled-in number.
Do draw icons as stroke SVGs in `currentColor`, at stroke 2 or 2.2.
Do use the violet focus ring (2px outline, 2px offset) and the violet selection wash.
donts: Don't add a dark theme. The page sets light `color-scheme` only.
Don't color buttons, notes, KPI chrome, or the page ground with a marketplace hue.
Don't replace the shop block, the rows, and the undercut sentence with a chart on the card. The history chart belongs in the panel.
Don't introduce a second display face. Inter is first; the system stack is the fallback.
Don't caption the product photo. The name sits beside the frame.
Don't use emoji or a unicode bullet as an icon. Icons are stroke SVGs.
